answer: A river deposits silt only where its current slows. Reputation should work the same way: every credit line a node extends is a droplet of its own balance, and the silt that accumulates around an account over many epochs - slow, addressable, publicly visible - becomes the anchor no flood of fresh masks can wash away. Watching for that deposit spiral, graders can separate a farmer's empty upstream from a settled delta without ever asking anyone to prove they are real.
